title: Eliminate the OS page cache: storage DMAs straight into app buffers
idea: Remove the kernel page cache entirely: file reads DMA directly from NVMe into application-owned buffers (io_uring fixed buffers), and any read caching moves into the SSD's own SLC region or a CXL-attached flash tier with a small SRAM line cache.
why: Page cache commonly holds 20-40% of server DRAM; eliminating it as a DRAM consumer frees that capacity at near-zero cost per bit.

title: Eliminate the stored KV cache: recompute K/V from residual checkpoints
idea: Instead of keeping K and V for every layer, store only the residual-stream vector every 8th layer per token and regenerate K/V for the intermediate layers on the fly during decode, using the FLOPs that sit idle in memory-bound decoding.
why: Attacks data movement and KV capacity: 4-8x less KV memory per session, turning a memory-bound phase into a compute-bound one on hardware with spare FLOPs.

title: Eliminate per-accelerator weight replicas via optical multicast weight broadcast
idea: Keep one copy of model weights in a pooled memory appliance and broadcast each layer's weights over a passive optical splitter to 8-64 accelerators that consume them in lockstep; local HBM holds only KV and activations.
why: Removes 8-64x duplication of weights across a serving pod; HBM per accelerator could drop 50-70%, easing the HBM TSV-tax bottleneck.

title: Eliminate storage for all-zero cache lines in the memory controller
idea: A per-page 64-bit presence bitmap in the controller marks zero 64B lines, which occupy no DRAM; nonzero lines are packed contiguously and the bitmap is cached on-chip, so a zero-line read costs no DRAM access at all.
why: Post-ReLU activations, sparse tensors and freshly allocated heaps are 30-60% zero lines: 1.3-2x effective capacity and fewer activations per useful bit.

title: Eliminate the decompressed copy: load units decode compressed formats natively
idea: CPU/GPU load-store units gain decoders for dictionary, delta and bit-packed columnar encodings, expanding values into registers, so DRAM only ever holds the compressed form and no decompressed working copy exists.
why: Analytics and columnar workloads get 2-4x effective DRAM capacity and proportionally less data-movement energy.

title: Eliminate fragmentation slack with transparent hardware object compaction
idea: The memory controller keeps a small redirection table and relocates live small objects in the background into dense pages, updating mappings like a hardware copying collector, so malloc arenas stop wasting free holes.
why: Long-running allocators waste 15-30% of DRAM to fragmentation; reclaiming it is pure capacity gain without app changes.

title: Eliminate stored weights: regenerate weight blocks from PRNG seeds
idea: Each weight block is replaced by a seed plus 4-8 coefficients that combine LFSR-generated pseudo-random basis vectors; banks of on-chip LFSRs regenerate the block at use time, so DRAM holds only seeds and coefficients.
why: 3-5x weight compression with no DRAM bandwidth for the regenerated part; attacks capacity and data-movement energy.

title: Eliminate redundant buffer copies with OS move-semantics page ownership
idea: The OS gains a linear-ownership primitive: a buffer moves from NIC to kernel to app to serializer by page remapping with the old mapping revoked, so a request path holds one copy of data instead of 3-4.
why: Network-heavy services hold 2-4 copies of each payload; collapsing them cuts buffer DRAM 50-75%.

title: Eliminate Adam optimizer state with moment-free sign updates
idea: Train with a sign-based optimizer whose only per-parameter state is a 1-bit error-feedback residual, removing the two fp32 moment tensors that Adam keeps for every weight.
why: Optimizer state is about 2/3 of mixed-precision training memory beyond weights; removing it cuts total training memory 40-60%.

title: Eliminate backprop activation storage via forward-only perturbation training
idea: Fine-tune with zeroth-order or forward-gradient estimates: two perturbed forward passes from a shared random seed estimate the gradient, so no activations are stored and memory equals the inference footprint.
why: Fine-tuning memory drops up to ~10x, so jobs that needed 8 GPUs of HBM fit on one.

title: Eliminate duplicate lines with content-addressed main memory in CXL expanders
idea: A CXL memory expander stores 64B lines by hash in a deduplicated store with reference counts; host physical addresses map to hash entries, so identical lines across VMs and containers are stored once.
why: VM and container fleets have 20-50% duplicate content: 1.25-2x capacity per installed bit.

title: Eliminate garbage-collector heap headroom with compile-time memory management
idea: Managed languages switch from tracing GC, which needs 2-5x heap headroom, to region inference plus precise reference counting with in-place reuse (Perceus-style) chosen by the compiler.
why: Heaps of Java/Go/C#-class services shrink 2-3x at equal throughput.

title: Eliminate object headers and pointers by compiling graphs into arenas
idea: A compiler pass converts pointer-linked object graphs into struct-of-arrays arenas addressed by implicit 32-bit indices, deleting per-object headers, 64-bit pointers and alignment padding.
why: Pointer-heavy heaps shrink 30-50%, and denser arrays also cut cache-line overfetch.

title: Eliminate SSD mapping DRAM fleet-wide with zoned flash placement
idea: Mandate zoned namespaces or flexible data placement across storage fleets, so the host writes log-structured and the SSD drops its page-level FTL map, which costs about 1 GB of DRAM per TB of flash.
why: Every exabyte of flash frees about 1 PB of DRAM, a large hidden demand cut while DRAM is 4x more expensive.

title: Eliminate recommender embedding tables with hash-driven embedding generators
idea: Replace TB-scale ID-to-vector tables with deep hash embedding: each ID is hashed by k functions into a dense code, and a small MLP generates its embedding on the fly.
why: Recommendation models are the largest DRAM consumers in many datacenters; tables shrink 100-1000x into GB-scale networks.

title: Eliminate linear KV growth with holographic superposed token memory
idea: Bind each old token's key/value pair to a random unit-phase vector and add it into a fixed-size complex matrix (holographic reduced representation); the newest N tokens stay exact and older ones are retrieved approximately by unbinding.
why: KV memory becomes O(1) in context length beyond a window: 10-100x savings for million-token contexts.

title: Eliminate sideband ECC bits for AI tensors using algorithmic checksums
idea: Put recomputable AI data on non-ECC channels and protect it with algorithm-based fault tolerance: row and column checksums on each matmul, with recompute on mismatch, so no memory ECC is needed for those regions.
why: Reclaims the 20-25% of RDIMM bits spent on ECC chips for the biggest DRAM consumer class.

title: Eliminate the full gradient buffer by fusing backward with update
idea: Apply each layer's optimizer update the moment its gradient is computed in the backward pass, then free that gradient immediately, so the full-model gradient tensor never exists (LOMO-style fused update).
why: Removes a weight-sized buffer from training memory, about 25% of the footprint in mixed precision.

title: Eliminate time-zone idle DRAM with follow-the-sun memory scheduling
idea: A global scheduler moves memory-heavy batch, training and offline-inference jobs across continents so each region's DRAM serves its local daytime peak and other regions' night-time batch load.
why: Fleet-average DRAM utilization rises from ~40% to ~70%, meaning 30-40% less DRAM must be bought for the same work.

title: Eliminate per-layer KV caches by sharing one KV across layer groups
idea: Train models where groups of 2-4 adjacent layers query one shared K/V projection stored once, with small per-layer query adapters for quality.
why: KV memory drops 2-4x architecturally, stacking with quantization and paging.

title: Eliminate the guest OS inside every VM with unikernel images
idea: Compile cloud services as unikernels or library OSes that link only the kernel functions they use, removing the 200 MB-1 GB guest kernel, init system and page cache that each VM duplicates.
why: Dense VM hosts carrying hundreds of guests recover 10-30% of host DRAM.

title: Eliminate unneeded mantissa bits with bit-plane tensor storage
idea: Tensors are laid out as separate bit planes; a profiler sets per-tensor error budgets and the planes below them are never written, while the memory controller fetches only the planes a kernel asks for.
why: Mixed workloads hold 1.5-3x more tensors per GB, with matching cuts in fetch energy.

title: Eliminate the raw object: cache media as neural latent codes
idea: Image, video-thumbnail and document caches keep learned latent codes from a neural codec instead of raw or JPEG bytes; an inline accelerator decodes them on access, with perceptual error bounds per tenant.
why: Media-heavy in-memory caches (CDN edge, social feeds) need about 10x less DRAM.

title: Eliminate fork's 2x memory peak with userfaultfd write-protect snapshots
idea: A 10-person team ships a library that replaces fork-based snapshots (Redis BGSAVE, Postgres-style checkpoints) with userfaultfd write-protection: the snapshotter streams pages to disk and copies only pages written mid-snapshot.
why: In-memory stores are provisioned at about 2x their data to survive fork copy-on-write storms; removing that cuts their DRAM by up to 45%.

title: Eliminate new DRAM purchases: CXL boards that re-home retired DDR4
idea: A small hardware team designs a CXL Type-3 card around an off-the-shelf CXL memory controller with 8 DDR4 slots and builds a test-and-bin line, turning DIMMs from decommissioned servers into a far-memory tier.
why: Avoids buying new DDR5 at 4x prices for cold tiers and gives ~5-year-old DRAM another 5 years of use, with no fab involved.

title: Eliminate system-prompt KV by baking fixed prompts into adapters
idea: Distill each tenant's long fixed system prompt or reference document into a tiny LoRA adapter through context distillation, so sessions carry no prefix KV at all; it ships as a software tool by a small team.
why: Prefix KV can be 10-50% of per-session memory in agent workloads; after baking, it is a few MB shared per tenant.

title: Eliminate full fine-tune copies with 1-bit deltas over shared bases
idea: Store each fine-tuned variant as the sign of its weight delta plus per-row scales relative to one resident base model, served by a fused dequant-add GPU kernel; it is a software product.
why: Serving 100 variants needs about 1.1x base memory instead of 100x, a 10-16x saving per variant.

title: Eliminate unused high bits with profile-guided field narrowing
idea: An LLVM plugin records observed value ranges of struct fields in production profiles, then shrinks int64 fields to 8/16/32 bits, bit-packs booleans and reorders fields to remove padding, with trap-on-overflow guards.
why: C/C++/Rust service heaps shrink 10-25% with a recompile.

title: Eliminate per-pod JVM headroom with a node-level elastic heap broker
idea: A sidecar daemon watches GC pressure across all JVMs on a node and, through GC tuning hooks and madvise, shrinks idle heaps and lends the freed pages to busy ones in real time, instead of each pod reserving its own peak.
why: Kubernetes Java fleets overprovision heap 1.5-3x; pooling headroom per node saves 25-40% of DRAM.

title: Eliminate 3x replication in memory caches using erasure coding
idea: A drop-in memcached/Redis cluster proxy stripes values with Reed-Solomon RS(10,4) across nodes and decodes on the client, replacing triple replication for durable caches.
why: Memory overhead for fault tolerance falls from 3x to 1.4x, a 53% DRAM saving.

title: Eliminate hash-table overhead with succinct minimal-perfect-hash cache modules
idea: A Redis module rebuilds read-mostly keyspaces into a minimal perfect hash (about 2 bits/key) plus Elias-Fano-packed values, with a small mutable delta table merged incrementally.
why: Pointer-rich hash tables cost 50-80 B/key of overhead; density improves 3-5x.

title: Eliminate host DRAM staging: GPU servers spec'd with quarter memory
idea: Use GPUDirect Storage loaders so weights and datasets go NVMe-to-HBM directly, and publish an open reference server spec with 256 GB host DRAM instead of 1-2 TB; it is a software plus integration business.
why: Host DRAM in AI servers, much of it staging buffers, is a large and growing DRAM sink; cuts of 4-8x per server are possible.

title: Eliminate idle-expert residency with one-layer-ahead MoE expert prefetch
idea: An open-source MoE runtime runs the next layer's router on the current hidden state to predict its experts one layer early and streams them over PCIe from host or NVMe, so HBM holds only about 25% of experts plus a hot cache.
why: MoE models need 3-4x less accelerator memory, which directly reduces HBM, the scarcest DRAM product.

title: Eliminate in-RAM float vectors from retrieval databases
idea: A vector database keeps only 1-bit quantized codes and graph adjacency in RAM and reranks the top candidates by reading full-precision vectors from NVMe; a small team can build it.
why: RAG vector indexes shrink 16-32x in DRAM, and these indexes are a fast-growing new DRAM demand.

title: Eliminate VFIO memory pinning with IOMMU page-fault passthrough
idea: A hypervisor patch set uses ATS/PRI page-request faults so GPU/NIC passthrough VMs stop pinning all guest memory, letting those VMs be overcommitted and ballooned like ordinary ones.
why: GPU clouds strand 20-40% of host DRAM because pinned VMs cannot share; this reclaims it.

title: Eliminate Python object boxing with tagged-pointer CPython build
idea: A drop-in CPython fork encodes small ints and floats as tagged pointers and stores homogeneous lists as unboxed typed arrays, keeping C-API compatibility through lazy boxing.
why: Numeric-heavy Python data pipelines use 2-4x less memory, recovering a large hidden DRAM consumer in ML preprocessing.

title: Eliminate peak provisioning with an internal revocable DRAM spot market
idea: A cluster agent sells revocable memory leases to batch jobs at a price set by node pressure, and reclaims leased pages within 100 ms by compressing them to zswap when the owner needs them back.
why: Raises cluster DRAM utilization from ~50% to ~80%, the equivalent of 35% more supply without new chips.

title: Eliminate DRAM from inference: model pipelined across FPGA SRAM boards
idea: A small team builds a chassis of off-the-shelf FPGAs linked by serial transceivers; each FPGA holds a slice of a quantized model entirely in its on-chip URAM/BRAM, and tokens stream through the pipeline with no external DRAM.
why: No DRAM or HBM in the bill of materials for small and mid models; all data movement is on-chip at about 0.1 pJ/bit instead of 3-20 pJ/bit.

title: Eliminate the separate swap tier: spare GPU HBM as host swap
idea: A daemon exposes the unused HBM of under-loaded inference GPUs as a compressed swap device for the host over PCIe peer-to-peer, and evicts it instantly when the GPU needs memory back.
why: Inference fleets average 30-50% unused HBM; turning that into host memory delays CPU DRAM purchases.

title: Eliminate per-worker model copies via shared read-only weight mappings
idea: A serving framework loads weights once as a read-only mmap of safetensors files shared by all CPU workers, and shares a single GPU copy across worker processes using CUDA IPC handles, instead of each worker loading its own.
why: Multi-worker CPU and GPU serving often duplicates weights 4-16x per node; collapsing them to one copy saves most of that.

title: Eliminate background app residency with compressed heap hibernation on clients
idea: A desktop OS service serializes the JS/V8 heaps of background browser tabs and Electron apps into zstd blobs on SSD and restores them lazily on focus, with sub-second resume.
why: Electron apps and tabs consume 300 MB-1 GB each; laptops could ship 8 GB instead of 16 GB and cut client DRAM demand.

title: Eliminate full-precision KV for stale tokens with age-tiered quantization
idea: An inference kernel library re-quantizes KV in the background as tokens age: the newest 512 tokens stay at fp16, older ones drop to int4, and the oldest to 2-bit with per-channel outlier rescue.
why: Long-context KV memory falls 4-6x with a small quality loss concentrated on distant tokens.

title: Eliminate parsed object trees: query JSON directly from raw bytes
idea: Services replace DOM-materializing JSON/protobuf parsers with SIMD on-demand cursors over the raw buffer (a structural-index tape), so no object tree is built in memory.
why: Parsed DOMs are 5-10x larger than their text; API gateways and log pipelines cut heap 3-8x.

title: Eliminate serverless warm pools with lazy snapshot-restored microVMs
idea: Idle function microVMs are snapshotted to NVMe; on invocation a userfaultfd handler restores pages lazily, prefetching a recorded working-set trace, to reach under 10 ms cold starts without keeping instances in RAM.
why: Warm pools keep 5-10x more instances resident than are executing; eliminating them cuts serverless DRAM by that factor.

title: Eliminate the zero-defect requirement: DIMMs from downgraded DRAM dies
idea: Buy DRAM dies that failed full-spec binning, assemble them into modules at a contract manufacturer with an on-module SPD map of bad rows, and have a Linux memmap/badram driver retire those pages at boot.
why: Recovers supply that fabs scrap or sell for scrap, at deep discount: 5-15% more usable bits from existing wafer output.

title: Eliminate stranded DIMMs: fleet profiling plus physical DIMM redistribution
idea: A 10-person service profiles fleet memory use with eBPF, finds hosts with chronically idle DIMMs, and sends technicians to move modules into memory-starved hosts during maintenance windows.
why: Fleets typically strand 20-30% of installed DRAM; reallocating it defers new purchases by a year or more.
